result:
There is a particular kind of quiet that only exists in the early morning, before the world has fully decided to wake up. It isn't silence exactly, but a softer version of sound — the hum of the refrigerator, the faint tick of a clock, the occasional bird testing its voice against the dark.

I like to sit in that quiet with a cup of coffee and watch the steam rise. It curls and vanishes and never repeats the same shape twice. It reminds me that most beautiful things are temporary by design. We are not meant to hold onto the steam, only to notice it while it is there.

For a long time I thought creativity had to be loud and dramatic, a lightning strike of inspiration. Now I think it is much more like tending a small garden. You show up even when you don't feel inspired. You water the soil, you pull the weeds, you wait. Some days nothing seems to grow. Other days you find something unexpected has bloomed overnight while you were sleeping.

Ideas are not so different. They drift in like seeds on the wind. Some land on concrete and fade. Some find soft earth and take root. Our job is not to control the wind, but to keep our patch of earth ready.

Maybe that is enough — to keep showing up, to notice the steam, to tend the garden, to trust that quiet work in dim light will eventually become something worth sharing.
